utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. Could we have the appearance for the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of General Enver Hadzihasanovic, Edina Residovic, counsel -- lead counsel; and Mr. Stephane Bourgon, co-counsel. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On behalf of Mr. Kubura, Rodney Dixon, Fahrudin Ibrisimovic, and Nermin Mulalic, our legal assistant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The Trial Chamber would like to greet everyone in the courtroom, members of the Prosecution, Defence counsel, the accused, and everyone else in the courtroom, including the interpreters, who are assisting us efficiently. We will be viewing some videos today, but before we do so, the Trial Chamber will render an oral decision. I will now ask the registrar to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in private session -- we are in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'll now turn to the Prosecution. We will continue with the viewing of the videos. But are there any questions the Defence would like to ask? You may take the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, could we go into private session very briefly again?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Registrar, we will go back into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll now give the floor to the Prosecution to address the issue of the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. [Interpretation] I have another semantic issue to deal with, and I will let Judge Swart question Mr. Dixon about the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Just a question of detail, Mr. Dixon. Yesterday you said when we saw the video with the former President Izetbegovic that there was a difference in B/C/S between the word "Mujahed" and "Mujahedin." If the original text we have seen -- in the two original texts the word "Mujahed" is being used and in the English translation the word "Mujahedin." You draw our attention to the difference, and you said basically these two words have fundamentally or importantly different meanings, but you didn't explain the difference. I would like to hear what is behind your remark.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, I didn't go into any detail, as I expected that this would become clearer through the evidence presented in the case and the Defence case. But, Your Honour, in a nutshell, the word "Mujahed," I'm informed, is a word which refers to a fighter and not necessarily a foreign fighter waging a holy war, which is what "Mujahedin" refers to, certainly in the way in which it's been referred to in the indictment brought by the Prosecution and also in the evidence presented by -- by the witnesses to date. And because of that distinction in the meaning, "Mujahedin" having a particular meaning relating to a fighter with a very specific cause in mind, it's because of that difference to the general term "Mujahed" which simply refers to a fighter that I wanted to draw the distinction in the translation and ensure that the English translation did match with the word that was used in the original Bosnian. But Your Honour, this will become more apparent during the course of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. trial. And I don't wish to myself give more evidence about the matter but simply to have it corrected for the record at this stage. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SWART
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. As far as this question is concerned, the Trial Chamber would also like to know about the existence of a word in B/C/S that would cover these two concepts. Is there a term in B/C/S that makes a distinction between a combatant and a combatant involved in a religious mission or some other sort of mission? Is there the terms in B/C/S that make this distinction, terms that we might be able to find in English but not in B/C/S?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, in the Bosnian language, there are quite a lot of words that come from the Arabic and Turkish language. "Mujahed" and "Mujahedin" are Arabic words. In Bosnian, "Mujahed," would be translated as "combatant." In Arabic "din" means "faith." If you add "din," the particle "din" to "Mujahed" in Arabic then this would be translated as a holy or religious combatant in our language. That's my understanding, although I am not an expert in languages. But this is how "Mujahed" and "Mujahedin" is translated in our country.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I -- if I could also add that all of the B/C/S witnesses who have come before Your Honours and testified about the presence of the Mujahedin in Bosnia, if the transcript is examined, they have used the word "Mujahedin" to describe the foreigners who were there in Central Bosnia. They have not used the word "Mujahed," and that's another reason why we wanted to -- to point out the distinction. There's no such word for "Mujahedin" in B/C/S other than "Mujahedin," but it has a particular meaning and that's the one that's been ascribed to by the witnesses who have come to Your Honours to date. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Mundis, does the Prosecution have any comments to make with regard to this semantic issue in order to clarify the matter for the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Not at this time, Mr. President. We may revisit the issue, but I don't anticipate we will need to do so. But we have nothing to add at this time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll continue viewing the videos now, and we'll pay particular attention to see whether the commentators used the word "Mujahedin" or if other persons in the video used this term, in order to see what the importance of this term is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Defence counsels. I first want to mention that this morning the Prosecution has handed over to the Defence two transcripts from the Kordic and Cerkez case relating to the first and to the fourth video shown yesterday. And after the break or at some later point in time we intend to turn to these transcripts. Secondly, the Prosecution has revisited the so-called reserve list and intends to raise in the course of the day another tape or the broadcasting of another tape with the Defence counsels and two other tapes are currently being checked, but at this point in time we cannot say anything about it. In the course of the day, probably at the end of the day, we will make an announcement. As it stands now, it's not -- in the course of the day, we will make an announcement about this. Then turning to the first tape this morning. It's the tape which is on your lists under number 2. It's V0003764, which is -- or the translation -- excuse me, the transcript is contained in tab number 1 of the binder. This tape has a duration of 113 minutes, close to two hours, and since it is 9.30 already, the broadcasting will be split up into two pieces at least, a first piece being shown now and a second piece being shown after the break. This exhibit -- or this videotape has been put into evidence already through the witness Zivko Totic on the 26th of February, 2004. It has the exhibit number P70. An excerpt from this tape has been put to the witness Zivko Totic, not the whole tape. The tape is probably from 1993. The Prosecution doesn't have particular information about it. Also, the author of this tape is not exactly clear. The submitter of this tape was Rida Attarashany, who in 1998 was spokesman for the OHR in Bosnia and for Carlos Westendorp, and this tape was handed over to the lead investigator of the ICTY, Peter Hackshaw, in December 2001. The content of this tape relates to paragraph 18 till 21 of the third amended version of the indictment. The tape will be shown now, if there are no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Would the Defence like to make any observations at this stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Good morning, Madam Judge. Good morning, Your Honour. Five minutes 30 seconds on the tape, the date of the 26th of May, 1995 appears; and also similarly, later on at seven minutes 11 seconds the date of the 15th of December, 1995 appears. So these dates, Mr. President, can be seen for a fraction of a second because the video is a montage or collage of videotapes. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON

Just one point, and that is, as the Prosecution has indicated, only a portion so far has been introduced into evidence because it was identified by the witness Mr. Totic. But as Your Honours will see, there's a compilation of so many different scenes in this tape taken from a range of different places, and that is why we contest it. Because as the Prosecution have indicated, we don't know who the author is and we don't know where half of these scenes come from, in the absence of a witness who could identify any of them. utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] -- for he knows that if Allah wills for a shell to hit us now, we would be all killed there. THE NARRATOR: [In English] Azam Publications UK presents it's first video cassette, "The Muslim [inaudible]," recording the historical events of the martyrs in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] When the Muslims heard this call and painful scream, several of the Islamic personalities, who felt concerned for the well-being of the being, and from those who waged Jihad in Allah's sake, moved towards the land of Bosnia. At the forefront of this movement were some of the brothers who are veterans of the Afghan Jihad. The Afghan Jihad, served as an institute for the teaching of Jihad, from which numerous militarymen and the Mujahedin leadership graduated, producing groups which played active roles with the will of Allah in the Jihad, and had an influence on the Mujahedin in different parts of the Muslim world. One month after the war started in 1992, the first group of the foreign Mujahedin arrived in the land of Bosnia and formed two Jihad camps. The first was in Central Bosnia. The second was situated in an area called Mehuric, which is close to the city of Travnik. There was also a presence of the Mujahedin brothers, in Turbe and Radina [phoen], which lie between Travnik and Doniva [phoen]. These efforts were carried out under the leadership of Sheikh Abu Abdel Aziz, who was one of the first people to arrive in Bosnia from the Arabian Peninsula. There he met the Mujahedin Shaheed Sheikh Anwar Sha'baan and together they agreed on the importance of initiating and carrying out the Jihad efforts in Bosnia, to give victory to the Muslims and repel the enemy aggressors. With regards to the military situation in Bosnia at that time, there existed the civilian armed force named the TO, in each area, responsible for the training and defending of the local inhabitants. And there was the Croatian HVO Defence Forces, comprising of Croatians and assisted by some Muslims. Agents from these forces were responsible for igniting and increasing the tensions in Bosnia. They undertook provocative operations that the Serbs were awaiting, in order to carry out their plans to form Greater Serbia and Greater Croatia, at the expense of the Muslims. The Muslims suffered a series of early defeats, due to their lack of war preparations, and the absence of an independent military leadership. Their presence amongst the ranks of the Croats, added to this, as the Croats possessed the necessary heavy military equipment, and the access routes to mainland Croatia, in order to fulfil their plans and ambitions. The Serbs possessed advanced weapons of the ex-Yugoslav army, at the period of time when the Muslims were in isolation, lacking even the simplest and most basic of military hardware and weaponry. As a result, they were forced to withdraw from the front lines, as will be narrated later on. The foreign Mujahedin were left with no option but to accept this unfortunate situation. The Mujahedin began by joining the civil defence units, due to the lack of an independent military leadership at that time. It also enabled them to become familiar with the geography of the local areas, to gain an understanding of the Bosnian people and to locate the enemy positions. The numbers of the Mujahedin began to increase day by day, with the Muslims coming from different and widespread locations. Groups of Mujahedin with previous Jihad and military experience from Afghanistan, began arriving in Bosnia. The Mujahedin then began teaching the Bosnian youth in Tesanj, to prepare them militarily, and teach them the Sariah, in order to wage a Jihad for the sake of Allah, in the correct manner. This caused the people to sit up, to take notice and to ask: "Who are the Mujahedins and why have they come to this land?" So fright and terror began to take root in the hearts of the Serbs. The Serbs were unable to take possession, and command of the areas, in which the Mujahedin were present, as in the case of Tesanj, and this was all due to Allah's will and blessing. Once the number of foreign Mujahedin had increased sufficiently, it was inevitable and necessary to establish a camp for the Mujahedin. The first camp for the military preparation and training was established in Mehuri. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] In August 1992, there was a vicious Serb offensive against the Muslims in Tesanj. The Serb objective was to take control of Tesanj and gain access to Central Bosnia. The Mujahedin played a prominent role, with the help of Allah, in repelling this Serb offensive. The Bosnian TO forces participated in repelling the offensive, and there were heavy Serb casualties despite an inequality in the weaponry and military preparations of the two sides. As a result of the heavy Serb shelling, some of the TO units left their positions. This led to the Mujahedin being frustrated and loosing their confidence in the Bosnian forces, due to the observations of the numerous defeats and withdrawals amongst their ranks. As a result, several of the foreign Mujahedin decided to go back to their countries. The patient ones remained, hoping for the rule of Allah, to [inaudible] and they continued patience through the difficulties and times of tribulation, all for the sake of Allah. During this period, Sheikh Abu Abdel Aziz, the leader of the Mujahedin in Bosnia, started to openly discuss the long-term effects of the Bosnian crisis and its importance, due to its situation, in the heart of Europe. He began to relay the news of the Jihad and the Mujahedin in Bosnia to the rest of the world. The prominent Islamic scholars in the world then began to give sermons and lectures on this issue. At the forefront of them were Sheikh Salman Al-Awdah and Sheikh Abdul-Majeed Az-Zindani, [inaudible] and other scholars, for whom the issue of Jihad has a high importance, Sheikh Omar Abdul-Rahman, Sheikh Omar Bin Ahmad Saif and Sheikh Abu Talal Al Qaasimi. Numerous young men from different Muslim countries, prepared themselves, and began to leave for the Jihad in Bosnia [inaudible] for a driving force, for the Jihad issued to arise in Europe due to the many efforts of the callers to Islam. At the head of them was Sheikh Anwar Sha'baan, may Allah have Mercy on him, who established summer training camps. In the summer of 1992, Sheikh Anwar arrived in Bosnia, with a group of brothers, to participate in a summer camp. It was at this time that the Mujahedin were planning and preparing for their first offensive Jihad operation against the Serbs. During the September 1992, the first Mujahedin offensive operation against the Serbs was carried out, under the leadership of the Bahraini Prince Muhammad Al-Faatih Al Bahraini, with Sheikh Anwar Sha'baan, as second in command. The Bosnian Muslim forces had been formed, and Allah willed for them to join the Mujahedin. A group of them participated in the operation. The Mujahedin moved towards the Serb front line, penetrating and gaining control over these areas, inflicting heavy defeats on the enemies of Allah. At this time the Bosnians did not have a complete understanding of the Islam, of [inaudible], and the understanding of why they were fighting. In addition to this, the limited military capabilities of the front line meant that they were unable to hold their positions due to the heavy Serbian shelling. Mohammad Al-Faatih Al Bahraini came from Bahrain to the land of Jihad in Bosnia, after he had abandoned the world of all its attractions. He was a prince of the royal family in Bahrain. He is married, however the responsibilities of married life did not prevent him from going to Jihad. His wife would encourage him to go for Jihad. He was also convinced of the need to go to the land of Bosnia by a dream, in which he was being called to Jihad in the mountains of the Balkans. At this time, he did not know what the Balkans were. Once his dream had been interpreted and he was informed that the Balkan mountains were in Bosnia and Herzegovina, he answered the call to Jihad and made his way to the Balkans. Mohammad Al-Faatih had participated in the Jihad of Afghanistan where he gained a high level of military experience. Brother Abu Sahar [phoen] from Egypt, who lived with Al-Faatih, said of him:

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] Abu Shareef was from the first people to arrive in the land of Jihad of Bosnia on the same ship that was carrying Al-Faatih, and Allah willed for them both to be killed in the first operation against the Serbs. Abu Shareef had participated in the Afghan Jihad. Then he moved to a European country. Upon hearing of the tragedy that had befallen the Muslims in Bosnia he answered the call of his Lord. As to the say in which he was killed after the death of Al-Faatih, in the physical operation the brothers decided to take his body away. Abu Shareef had the responsibility of providing cover for the brothers with a PK machine-gun whilst they were removing Al-Faatih's body. Then Abu Shareef was hit by a piece of shrapnel on his arm, and a moment later he was hit by a mortar shell which killed him and Abu Anas Al-Jeddawi so they joined their brother Al-Faatih. May Allah have Mercy upon them. This story reminds us of a poet's saying: "Whoever's death is written in a certain land, then he would not die in a land other than it." He graduated from the Afghan Jihad after fulfilling his duty there. He then arrived in Bosnia in order to help his Muslim brothers gain victory. He was renowned for his cheerfulness, his pleasant character and his jokes that did not exceed the limits of the Shariah. All the brothers loved him. One of the brothers, Abu Sahar says of him:

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] He participated in the Jihad of Afghanistan but was not bestowed with the honour of Martyrdom there. So Allah willed for him to join the caravan of Martyrs in the land of Bosnia after receiving a direct hit from a piece of shrapnel in his face which resulted in his immediate death. We consider him from the Shokadah [phoen] with the will of Allah. In addition to the prominent role played by the Arabs in the Bosnian Jihad, the non-Arabs also had a key role in the Jihad. In this operation, Abdullah from Albania and Abdul-Majeed from Turkey were also killed. They came from their respective countries to participate with the Muslims in their Jihad against the enemies of Allah. We ask Allah to accept them both from the Shokadah. In October 1992, a group of Mujahedin carried out an operation to liberate Sarajevo airport from the surrounding Serbs. The disbelieving United Nations forces amongst them soldiers from the Egyptian army, intervened in repelling this attack. Two brothers, Abdul-Abbas and Abu Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Zubair [phoen], both from Madinah [phoen], were killed in this operation. May Allah have Mercy upon them. The French United Nations shot and killed Ibrahim from Britain, one of the brothers who was on his way to Sarajevo. His body was found near Sarajevo airport after a Bosnian Mujahedin had witnessed his killing. They also killed two students, a Syrian, and an Algerian, in Sarajevo. At this stage it became apparent the cunning role that the international forces were playing. They always protected the Christians and hunted the Muslims, because all disbelievers only stay loyal to each other. It was not possible for the problems of the Muslims to be solved at a conference table of the disbelievers. When we come to mention the memories of Muhammad Al-Habashi [phoen], Abu Zubair and Fadil Al-A'Idee Abul-Abbas [phoen]. It was sorrow upon sorrow into our hearts at the loss of these dear two brothers.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] Operation "Bilizna" took place on the 7th November 1992. The Muslims recaptured Mount Bilizna that overlooked Zavidovici. The Serb forces had been entrenched on this mountain, from where they shelled the town, day and night. Due to the strategic nature of this mountain, the Serbs fought hard to recapture it, but eventually it was in the hand of the Muslims. As events progressed, the Serbs continued to shell the Muslim towns and villages, in a barbaric manner, until the Muslim city of Jajce fell to the Serbs, in November 1992, as a result of a clear betrayal by the Croats. Croatia was to sole route of entry into Bosnia. As a result of this, the Croats began to provoke the Muslims, in particular the Mujahedin, passing through their lands. They stole, looted and pilfered from the convoys. Throughout the war, they looted in excess of a hundred million dollars from the Muslims, in addition to the beatings, torture and imprisonment. In spite of this, Mujahedin avoided confrontation with the Croats, so as to avoid opening new fronts of attack onto themselves and to maintain the route of entry and exit through Croatia. On the 29th December 1992, the second Visoko Operation was carried out, under the command of the Egyptian Abu [inaudible]. The Mujahedin moved from the frontline of Bijelo Bucje, near Travnik, to the mountains. These are the mountains that overlook the city of Ilijas, which is five kilometres away from Sarajevo. The mountains were liberated, and the Mujahedin continued advancing until they reached some difficult territory. There was then an aerial attack carried out by the Serbs with the use of helicopters. The fighting continued from the morning until the time of the [inaudible]. The enemy were defeated, vast areas were liberated, and the city of Ilijas nearly fell into the hands of the Mujahedin. The Bosnian forces were not able to maintain the positions again, and the Arab brothers found themselves deserted in vast areas, so they were forced to withdraw. A large number of the brothers were injured and seven of the foreign Mujahedin were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] He was a student of knowledge who graduated from the Islamic University of Medine [phoen]. He preferred martyrdom in Allah's sake, to the certificate of this world and its false position. He left his studies to carry out the Jihad in the lands of the Balkans, to implement what he had learned. He was the commander of the Arabs, in the Second Visoko Operation, due to his good manners and character, and good dealings with the brothers, and his knowledge of the Shariah. One of the brothers recalled the events surrounding Abu Talha's death.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] Abu Mahmood of Palestine personified the saying of the hope: "I will sacrifice my soul, I will throw myself for towards death. There is either the noble life which pleases others, or a death which puts fear into the enemies." Abu Mahmood of Palestine was studying medicine in France. Then Allah willed for him to become a practising muslim. So he left France with his French friend Abu [inaudible] in order to wage Jihad in Bosnia. After two months of his stay in Bosnia, he decided to return to France. He stayed in Zenica for two days, awaiting the time of departure, but Allah had chosen a different journey for him, to the everlasting paradise of palaces and beautiful maidens. The Algerian brother Abu Muhaijir tells us how Abu Mahmood was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] After the one has tasted the sweetness of Jihad, he cannot take pleasure in the worldly life. There we have Abu Maryam al Afghani, who lived in Germany with his German wife, calling people to Islam. There he led a good life with all its comfort, but there is a difference between the one who has devoted to worldly life and the one who has embraced it. Abu Maryam, the Afghani, had previously participated in the Afghan Jihad, and in Germany he was extensively involved in dau [phoen] programs, calling people to Allah. When Abu Maryam, decided to return to Jihad, his parents stood in the way. So his wife spoke with his parents, convincing them about the importance of his going to the Jihad in Bosnia. This reminds us of some of the wives, of the noble companions of the Prophets of Allah, [inaudible], who encouraged their husbands to go for Jihad. So Abu Maryam travelled to Bosnia, together with his best friend and companion Abu Hudaifah al Afghani, who was also his work colleague. [inaudible] bestowed the two of them with acts in his obedience, reputation of the Koran, beautiful characters and eagerness in the service of their fellow Mujahedins. Abu Maryam used to clean the toilets and washed the dishes at times of extreme cold. His guarding of the front line, was a preparation for the Second Visoko Operation. And so Abu Hudaifah, asked the permission of his commander, to participate in this operation, with Abu Maryam. And in the beginning of the operation Abu Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Maryam was killed. It was only a few moments later that his brother, Abu Hudaifah joined him. How many are the people that seek fame and wealth today. And what of someone who has left all that in pursue of Allah's pleasure. Abul-Harith was a famous football player in Bahrain. A lot of the youth today yearn to attain his level of playing. He left his football career behind him and left for Afghanistan to take part in the Jihad, seeking to die in the path of Allah. He then went to participate in the Jihad in Bosnia. He had devoted his heart and his soul for the worship of Allah, and he set a good example with his manners and manhood. He was always seen reading the Koran, serving his brothers, and guarding the frontline. He was characterised by a smile that never left his face and a level of patience such that he never became angry at his brothers. He personified the saying of the Prophets of Allah: "A smile to your brother is a form of charity." A few days before the operation, Abul-Harith was seen to take great care of himself and he wore his best clothes, as if he knew that he had an appointment with the beautiful women of Paradise. When the battle had reached its most intense stage and the souls of the martyrs had been raised, Abul-Harith found Abu Maryam spread on the ground, his soul had been raised. He kissed him and said: "Oh, Allah, join us with him. He advanced towards the enemy from an area providing little cover, and while he was crawling on the ground, he was hit by a sniper bullet and he surrendered his soul to his Lord. The land of the Ottoman has not left out from sending volunteers from its youth to participate in the Jihad for Allah's sake. This response from the Turks was to be expected, since Turkey was the capital of the last Islamic Palace. Imraan from Turkey went to Bosnia to fight the enemies of Allah. He was 27 years old, of Turkish origin, and was living in America. He undertook the necessary military training, and after two months, he had the intention to return to America with a young orphan child who he wanted to adopt. He stayed with his Palestinian brother Abu Muhammad [phoen] in Zenica, awaiting his time of departure when news of the high alert situation reached him, and he preferred to stay than to travel, and he answered the call, so that he could meet his Lord and be free from the suffering and the pressures of this world, and to be free of living amongst the disbelievers in America. At the beginning of 1993, Sheikh Abu Abdel Aziz was forced to leave Bosnia to explain the situation to the scholars and to collect donations to assist in the Mujahedin. The leadership of the Mujahedin was handed over to Wahiudeen, the Egyptian. After Abu Abdel Aziz's departure, the Croats cut the routes used by the Muslims and those used particularly by the Mujahedin. They captured numerous Mujahedin who had ventured into hostile territory. From amongst those captured were: Abu Maiz and Abu Ali the Kuwaiti. They also killed Abu Sahar, may Allah have Mercy on him, and threw his body onto the roadside. This was the last straw, and the Mujahedin then began preparing a plotting to confront the Croats, the enemies of Allah. Mujahedin split themselves into three groups. The first group was in the village of Mehuric and responsibility was to carry out provocative measures against the Croats, and to monitor the Croatian forces. The second group was in Bijelo Bucje, and their task was to occupy the Croats in this area and attempt to take hostages. The third group was in Zenica, and their main function was to kidnap figures from the Croatian leadership. The brothers met to discuss how to release prisoners held by the Croats. The issue was discussed with the Bosnian Muslim forces, but there was no response. They also raised the issue with the UN, but they were not interested, because they are not interested in the affairs of the Muslims. [inaudible], the Egyptian, suggested that the only solution was for the group in Zenica to kidnap the leader of the Croatian HVO forces and to exchange him for the Mujahedin held in captivity. An agreement was made with the Commander of the Muslim forces in Travnik to send a group of his best soldiers tojoin the ranks of the Muhahedin to train them to carry out special operations. [inaudible] needed a special camp for this objective, so a new stage of rigorous training commenced, with particular attention being paid to matters relating to the sound and correct understanding of fighting in the path of Allah. After the completion of the training and gathering of information and necessary preparation, the Mujahedin were divided into groups. The first group kidnapped four Croat intelligence officers in Novi Travnik. The second group kidnapped the vice-commander of the Croat forces in Bosnia, along with six Croat soldiers. The news of the kidnaps spread quickly, and the disbelieving United Nations began to search for the kidnappers. They blockaded the roads and began to search everywhere. This meant that the brothers had to remain and hide in the forests, despite the snow, the intense cold, and the loss of communication with the Command Centre in Mehuric. The plight of the Mujahedin prisoners did not concern the UN, clearly illustrating their hypocrisy. The UN accused the Mujahedin of being terrorists and war criminals. The command then came from the Bosnian army to release the Croatian prisoners, but it was not obeyed. The next day, whilst the Commander of the Croatian forces was driving to work in Zenica, the Mujahedin blocked off his route from the front, and behind him, with the objective of taking him and those with him as prisoners. But his personal bodyguards started firing at the Mujahedin. The Mujahedin sprayed the car with gunfire killing everyone inside with the exception of one person, and here Allah's Will was demonstrated, in that the Croat Commander remained alive, and what was written by Allah happened. During this period, brothers gathered to debate and discuss the recent events and, Wahiudeen, may Allah have Mercy upon him, handed over the leadership to Dr. Abul Harith, from Libya, due to him having the necessary qualifications and the characteristics for this role. This gave Wahiudeen more time to concentrate on military affairs. Abul Harith took over the leadership of the Mujahedin in Zenica. Dr. Abul Harith approached the Muslim forces and asked them to inform the world of the kidnap operation, but they failed to do anything. Abul Harith then approached the UN forces present in Zenica. There was a great uproar, and the disbelieving United Nations moved quickly now attaching high priority to this issue. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Negotiations then took place, concerning the prisoner exchange, under the supervision of Wahiudeen, and [inaudible], in the rank of the Mujahedin. In May of 1993, the prisoner exchange took place. It was a historical event, which will never be forgotten, and the brothers being released from the Croatian prisons, and their feet touching the land of the Jihad once again. The brothers prostrated to Allah, upon their release, thanking Allah.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] After the prisoner exchange, the Croats declared open war against the Muslims in Bosnia, and in particular, the Mujahedin. They took control of the mountains in the Mehuric area and blocked off the main roads under their control, such as the Zenica-Travnik road. They were preparing to capture the towns of Zenica and Travnik, to surround the Mujahedin. This period was one of the most difficult periods for the Mujahedin in the war, with loss of communications between the groups in Mehuric, Zenica, and Travnik. This led to the Mujahedin not receiving any news or help. It therefore became necessary to open a new route into Travnik, and the Mujahedin attacked and captured the Croatian village of Miletici near Mehuric killing all the fighters and taking women and children as prisoners, to be handed to the Bosnian army. They also blew up the bridges connecting the Croatian villages to each other in order to isolate them as preparation before the capture of the village of Guca Gora, which is the historically significant village to the Croats. This is due to the presence of a large church in Guca Gora where delegations used to come from all over Europe, take part in wild parties, and offered the Croatians monetary assistance in their fight against the Muslims. The Guca Gora operation was one of the first signs of victory from Allah to the Mujahedin who had remained patient during this period of being surrounded. The village was captured and vast areas fell into the control of the Mujahedin, after opening the road from Zenica to Travnik. The Mujahedin also took a lot of war booty, capturing two heavy 120-millimetre mortars. This was the first time the Mujahedin had gained access to this sort of weapon. They also captured a lot of ammunition. After capturing Guca Gora, the Mujahedin advanced to capture a fortified mountainous area, under the leadership of Usama [inaudible], may Allah have Mercy on him, in order to capture the town of Vitez. The Croats were encamped, in their trenches behind these mountains. They fired at the Muslims, in a fearsome manner, leading to a large number of the Mujahedin getting injured, forcing the Mujahedin to withdraw, in order to limit their losses. Jamaludeen, from Yemen, and Muhammad the Turk, were killed, may Allah accept them from the martyrs. The messenger of Allah [inaudible] say: "Paradise has one hundred graves, which Allah had reserved for the Mujahedin who fight for His cause, and the distance between each of the two graves, is like the distance between the Heaven and the earth." The land of Yemen sent some of its precious sons to perform Jihad for the sake of Allah. The lands of Jihad, Afghanistan and Kashmir, saw many martyrs, originating from Yemen. Today we have, a [inaudible] Jamaludeen, a young man who was not more than 20 years old, who had dreamt of the [inaudible] and Paradise, whilst he was in Afghanistan. Allah willed for him to travel to the land of Jihad in Bosnia, to achieve his mission. Abu Uthman the Kuwaiti, speaks to us about Jamaludeen's dream.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] Muhham the Turk was a man who had been given strength by Allah, yet he was of gentle heart. He was easy and gentle amongst his brothers, yet harsh and severe against the enemies of Allah. He was from the first few people to attack the Croatian positions in the Guca Gora Operation. He killed six Croats and then joined his brothers in surrounding the Croats, who had taken refuge in the church. During the stand off, he was responsible for providing cover to the brothers, along with Jamaludeen, using the dashaka [phoen] machine-gun. A mortar bomb landed close to them, may Allah have Mercy upon them both. The Mujahedin leadership got together to establish the reasons for the defeats and the withdrawals. They found that the main reason was the lack of correct and sound Islamic belief amongst the members of the Bosnian army. In addition to this, there were traitors amongst the ranks of the army, a lack of good military planning and chaotic organisation, during the operations. The Shura Council for the Mujahedin decided to stop taking part with the army in any of the military operations until the Mujahedin were recognised as an independent battalion within the Bosnian army. The Bosnian army acknowledged the role that the Mujahedin had played so far and their need for men of this kind. Therefore the Bosnian army leadership agreed to their request and recognised the Mujahedin Battalion as a part of the Bosnian army, over which the banner of [inaudible] could be raised. This gave them the ability to choose their soldiers based on the Islamic Sharia. Thus began a new stage in the war with an increasing responsibility and a need for planning and organisation. The Head Office for the Battalion was in Zenica. The training camp was [inaudible] training camp, in the village of Mehuric. The leader of the battalion was Abul-Harith, the Libyan, may Allah have Mercy upon him, and the military commander was Wahiudeen, may Allah have Mercy upon him. From this point, the Mujahedin launched their first operation after the recognition of their battalion. This operation occurred in the summer of 1993 under the leadership of [inaudible], in the mountains surrounding the town of Vitez, which is inhabited by the Croats, and is close to the town of Novi Travnik. The loss of [inaudible] enabled the Mujahedin to capture this area, and they killed approximately forty Croats. From the Mujahedin, Abu Ali the Kuwaiti, and the Bosnian brother, Hamdu [phoen], were killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] The current state of affairs in the army in power in the Muslim countries is one of subservience, to oppressive puppet regimes, manufactured by the disbelieving west, in compete contradiction Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. to the Sharia, Allah [inaudible]. Thousands of soldiers and the wide array of advanced military technology and hardware, on which millions of dollars have been spent, have been reserved for military displays and, the official state's receptions, for the leaders of these countries. This military power is not used to maintain the honour and the dignity of the Muslims, nor is it used to defend the Muslim lands. Instead, we see these countries arguing amongst each other and directing their forces against each other. These forces should be directed against the enemies of Allah, such as the Jews and their supporters. The good people are those who are aware of these regimes and are aware of their corruption, and that the regimes are not established on Allah's Sharia. Such regimes have declared enmity to them, in order that they may proceed on the path of Allah. This is illustrated to us by the example of Abu Ali, a Kuwaiti who was an officer in the Kuwaiti army. He was sent to France as a part of a military delegation to receive training in artillery. On his return, Allah opened his eyes and his ears to what he had heard from Abu Abdul-Azeez who was calling and urging the youth, to go to the Jihad in Bosnia. He left his post in the armed forces, his wife, and his children, and he answered the call. After joining the Mujahedins, he began a new part in his life, the life of a Mujahedin. He was very obedient and attentive, modest and helpful to his brothers, always eager to solve their problems. The Kuwaiti army had called him back several times, and warned him that they may fire him. He refused to return. How could he return once he had tasted the pleasures of Jihad, and the defence of the front line. He was aware of the saying of the Prophets of Allah [inaudible]: "One hour spent in the path of Allah is better than performing night prayer, in [inaudible], at the Black stone of the [inaudible]."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] After the first Vitez operation, preparation was undertaken for the Croshitsa Operation. This attack was aimed at the western side of Vitez, in the vicinity of an explosives factory. It was carried out under the command of Wahiudeen. The Croats were defeated, and the Mujahedin were forced to stay in the area for the whole day. Due to the failure of the Bosnian army, the Mujahedin were forced to withdraw, and [inaudible] received a serious injury, whilst the Bosnian brother Ahmed was killed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] We're going to talk about the Shehids now. I remember Emir Potrapaca ,when he came to our unit. He was a young man, not more than 18 years old. He was a very peaceful, calm brother, who showed a lot of wisdom, always mentioning Allah's name. He fasted a lot, and always had a smile on his face. He made available everything he had for the assistance of the Jihad and the Mujahedin. He took the path of Jihad, following the way of [inaudible] Aziz. He arrived in Bosnia, at an early stage, and inflicted large losses on the enemies of Allah, in the numerous battles in which he participated, until his time came, and he was killed by the Croats, may Allah have Mercy on him.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] The Land of Jihad are most in need of those people of knowledge, who belief in implementing, what they have learned. Abu Abdur-Rahman, from Egypt, was in his thirties, and a student of the Islamic University in Medinah. He came to the Land of Jihad, early in the conflict, answering the cause. He participated in fighting the Crusaders, and was injured in Operation [inaudible]. He was from amongst the special group that carried out the kidnapping of a leader of the Croatian forces. He married in the Land of Jihad. He had not been married for more than eight months, and he was killed, shouting "Allahu Akhbar, Allahu Akhbar", and firing his machine gun upon [inaudible]. A member of Qatar national handball team, Abu Khalid, a Qatary, abandoned his world and came to Bosnia to fight in the path of Allah. He was known for his bravery and for his severity in dealing with the enemy of Allah. He showed great courage during Operation Croshitsa. He used his PK machine-gun to fire at the enemy until they received orders to withdraw. He continued preparing himself and defending the frontline until Allah chose him for the patience that he had shown, awaiting his reward from Allah. Abu Khalid El Qatary, once said: "I bought some clothes for which to go to Afghanistan, but my mother prevented me from going to Afghanistan, but insha-Allah, with these same clothes I will soon be killed in Bosnia. He was killed whilst firing on the Croats, along with Wahiudeen, the Egyptian, and his brothers, may Allah have Mercy upon them all.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: THE NARRATOR: [In English] The man who bears the responsibility of his religion and strives [inaudible]. They are unique example, selling their precious soul, to make Allah's work high and so that the religion everywhere, is only for Allah. The Land of Jihad throughout the world, have given us men of this nature, who've reached the top of their sacrifices in Jihad, for the sake of Islam, and who gave their blood in this path. Wahiudeen, the Egyptian, is an example of such men. Despite his relatively young age, he was able to accept the responsibility. Practising what you have learnt and sacrificing in the path of Allah, change personalities and creates unique types of individuals. This should not be surprising for us, since Osama Bin [inaudible] May Allah be pleased with him, was Commander of the Muslim army, when he was 18 years old, and companion of the Prophets of Allah, [inaudible], of the light of [inaudible], may Allah be pleased with him, were under his command. Allah helped the servants, according to the love of sacrifices for Islam, to make them the best of people. Wahiudeen was born in Southern Egypt, and he died in the land of Bosnia. He memorised the Koran from a young age, leading to a maturity in thinking. He was brought up amongst the children of the Islamic Movement in Egypt, and he became aware of the Islamic issues around the world. His thinking became occupied with their problems, and he always used to wonder how the Islamic caliphate could return to the Muslims. Wahiudeen then knew that it was necessary to go to Afghanistan, to achieve this ambition. There he joined a training camp. He began to prepare himself, and to train as hard as he could, learning how to use different types of weapons, and improving his physical fitness, with the Koran never leaving his side Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in this period. Wahiudeen showed excellence early on, which led to his trainer Al Bahari [phoen] taking notice of this young man. He began to concentrate on him in the training sessions, as if he was preparing him to fulfil the needs of the Muslims, for a man of his example. Having completed his training, he was then chosen to train the new brothers and he had outstanding achievements in fulfilling his task. He continued to work in the path of Allah, seeking martyrdom, following the news of the battles, moving towards the front lines, and experiencing intense fighting, in order to gain Allah's protection from the [inaudible]. He moved between the mountains and valleys of Afghanistan, participating in numerous operations, which implanted in him a desire to be a good soldier, and develop his Islamic leadership qualities. He was a cheerful person, well mannered, military minded, and mindful of his duties to Allah [inaudible], in terms of his acts of worship. When the Bosnian situation arose, Sheikh Anwar Sha'baan met with leading personalities from the Afghan Jihad, and they agreed to the importance of ensuring that men such as Wahiudeen, Mutazu Billah, and Husaamudeen went to Bosnia to initiate the Jihad efforts there. Wahiudeen met Sheikh Abu Abdul Aziz in Bosnia. Abu Abdul Aziz gave Wahiudeen responsibility for the military operations of the Mujahedin, due to what was known of his ability and experience in this field. He began to think about how to undertake and carry out the Jihad in Bosnia, through an organisation controlled by the Sharia, and by the fact that he was one of those holding a position of responsibility in the Mujahedin Battalion. He married in Bosnia, and he was killed by the Croats before seeing his daughter, who is now five years old. We send out greetings to you Wahiudeen, we ask Allah to unite us to the Prophets, the martyrs, the truthful people, and the [inaudible] People, what a beautiful friendship that is.
