utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Before I give the floor to Defence, I will briefly summarise what the Judges have seen and the conclusions they have been able to draw. First of all, as far as the dates are concerned, Mr. Bourgon said that there were two dates that we could see very briefly. He said -- he mentioned the 27th of May and the 15th of December, 1995. But there were other dates that appeared: The 5th of December, 1993, which appeared when there was an operation near Novi Travnik; and there was also a date which corresponds to the second operation in Vitez. We can also see that there was another date, in that at a certain point in time it was said that the daughter of the Mujahedin commander, the Egyptian Wahiudeen, was five years old. As this person died in 1993, if that's five years, that takes us to 1998, and in the video we can see the little girl who's five years old. So perhaps the year 1998 is the year in which this video was made. The quality of the video is good and it is in colour. As to who made the video, we can see a logo in Arabic, which appears to the right, and this video is usually either in the Arabic language or in English, so the purpose of the video was to be broadcast to an international audience. And at the end of the video, we noted that the title of the video was indicated. The title was "The martyrs of Bosnia." But it said "Part 1," so there is certainly a second part that should be the sequence, because the title of this video was "The martyrs of Bosnia, Part 1," so it should be followed by a second part. We also noticed that there is a juxtaposition of various sequences, either of combat sequences, of sequences showing training, and there were also sequences, scenes that were filmed apparently in Afghanistan. In addition, there are images that come from various sources, international sources such as the UN, international meetings, and from other sources. Much of the video portrays the Mujahedin's combat, and they've been described as martyrs. At the end we see the names of the martyrs, and there were about 30 of them. These martyrs - that's how they were described in the video - we see them, either photographs of them or videos, we can see their burials, because they were killed in combat. We also sometimes see them in combat sequences. Abu Khalid El Qatari can be seen in combat, and we can also see some of them who were -- or most of them who were killed in combat. And there are two specific things that appear; either the body shows traces of multiple wounds, which could be the result of explosions, or we can see bodies with traces of gunshot wounds. We can also see that the testimony of the friends of these martyrs, of these combatants, usually states that they were killed by snipers. In addition, we should point out that one of the martyrs, Abul-Harith, from Kuwait, seems to be involved in the exchange of Totic for the Mujahedin combatants, because we see him appear during this exchange, and afterwards there is a scene which shows him after he was killed. In addition, the video depicts events that relate to Miletici, and in Guca Gora we can see soldiers in the interior of the Guca Gora church. We could also see that there was some damage to the interior of the church but it wasn't extensive damage. So this is what we could say about Guca Gora. There is also a scene depicting training in Mehurici, since we're able to see the Mujahedin in this training camp in Mehurici. There was also a scene involving the exchange -- or depicting the exchange of Totic in Zenica for other combatants, and we saw a lot -- there was a lot more information than the information we saw in the photographs produced by the Defence, and one could draw the conclusion that there was much more information. There was also a report on a Mujahedin training camp on Mount Igman, and towards the end - and this also concerns the holy war - there were certain presentations or interviews involving a number of religious leaders, well-known individuals, such as the Sheikh Rahman, the Egyptian, Sheikh Madani from Algeria, or Sheikh Yaseen, from Palestine. So very briefly, this would be a summary of what we were able to see. But the Defence will also inform us of what they have to say. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. I don't want to take too much time to make comments which are divided into three parts but refer to three different sources. First of all, where the video was obtained from; how it was conserved, how it was preserved; and also, there is the question of the reliability of the video. I'll divide my comments into two parts. First of all, I will deal with the images and then the text, or the part narrated by the narrator. First of all, as far as the images are concerned, Mr. President, in the video in its totality no individuals and no one -- they're not included in the evidence in this case, unless it has to do with certain international persons, and there are no links to the indictment in this case, or if it's not a matter of Mr. Totic. When we see the photographs and the names of the people in the photographs who were mentioned in the video, we don't know whether the person that we see in fact bears the name mentioned in this video, the name that's supposed to correspond to the image. To be more specific, as far as the scene concerning the exchange in Zenica is concerned, we could recognise Commander Totic. We were able to see a certain link between the images shown and the photographs presented by the Defence, and the Trial Chamber has pointed this out. We have perhaps certain information about the date when this scene was made, and this is probably the reason for which the Prosecution wanted to present this scene and the Defence made a submission and didn't object to having this precise scene, this specific scene being admitted into evidence. As far as the other images that we could see are concerned, we don't know any of the places, apart from the place involved in the Totic exchange and the Guca Gora monastery. And again -- yet again, Mr. President, when speaking about the Guca Gora monastery, the photographs taken in the interior -- were taken in the interior of this monastery, or perhaps in some other monastery, but we really do not know who the individuals in this monastery or in this other building, we do not know [as interpreted]. And the faces were distorted by those who made the video. We do not know when these images were shot. That's the most important thing. And what we have heard in the course of these proceedings to date is that there were events in Guca Gora on the 9th and 10th of June. And it seems that there were Croats who had taken refuge in the monastery. We know, according to the evidence we have had, that there was no damage to the interior, and in the testimony of Kent-Payne and Bower, we know that there was -- that at an earlier date, which wasn't specified, there was a group of Mujahedin near the monastery. But on the basis of the images we have seen, we can't create a link between what we can see and the evidence that has been presented to date. Many images weren't shot in Bosnia - at least, that's what -- how it seems - and there are images of soldiers, but we can't determine whether they belong to a particular unit. The only common denominator seems to be a cry which is in evidence, so it appears that these are soldiers of Muslim origin and they have this cry or exclamation in common. As far as the weapons that we can see, they had a number of weapons. We don't know which forces possessed these weapons. We can also see a number of modern weapons, which probably weren't in use in the year 1993. That's what I wanted to say about the images that we can see, Mr. President. As far as the date when the video was made, we don't know when this took place; although, the Trial Chamber mentioned the daughter of one of the individuals and mentioned when the daughter was born. Naturally, this depends on the reliability of the narrator. The person who produced the video, who put together these various sequences, are not known. The reason for which the video was produced, we have certain indications about the reason from the narrator, but we don't know whether it's a matter of propaganda, whether it's dedicated to the martyrs, or homage to the martyrs, we don't know whether it's an instrument to recruit Mujahedin. We know nothing about this. We don't know who provided the video to the person mentioned by the Prosecution. This person has not testified before the Trial Chamber, the person who worked for the Bureau of the High Representative. We don't know how this person received the cassette, we don't know when, we don't know who provided the cassette to an investigator from the OTP, who has not testified either, and in a number of images we can see we note that these images come from international television channels and some also seem to be from the region of Bosnia. This has to do -- these comments have to do with what we saw. And now I'll talk about what we heard, Mr. President. The people who are speaking in the video are not identified, the people who drafted the text are not identified. There is often no relation or link between the narration of the events and the persons or the events that we can see in the video. And if there is a link, we don't know what the link is, because it's not even a testimony; it's a commentary, in fact. So to accept this narrative part of the video, Mr. President, it's obvious that we would need a witness who would be cross-examined so that we could check credibility and reliability. There are certain elements in -- certain elements in the video, certain events which have been mentioned, but nothing enables us to establish a relationship, a link between what we saw and what we heard. For these reasons, Mr. President, we don't think that this video has any reliability that would allow the Trial Chamber to admit it into evidence, apart from the scene depicting the Totic exchange, and that is already in evidence, and the Defence has no objections to this scene. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. I'll now turn to the other Defence team. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. A few additional comments. Your Honours, Mr. Bourgon is absolutely correct in making a distinction between the narration on the video and the images that are seen. In respect of the narration, our view is quite clear that it really is a witness statement. The narrator is giving an account of events and interpretation of events, and one which might be of some interest, but in our view should not be admitted into evidence unless that person was available to be cross-examined by the Defence and to be questioned by Your Honours. In relation to the images themselves, it may be, Your Honours, Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that there are some images that speak for themselves; the picture of Mr. Totic, for example, who has testified as a witness before Your Honours, and that -- in that sense the video is self-authenticating for those particular portions. But even for -- for some of those, and those that surround the -- the parts that might seem to be reliable, Your Honours, we would submit that it is necessary to obtain a witness to verify what is seen on those videos, and the Prosecution has had an opportunity to do this certainly in relation to the Totic exchange. A number of the international witnesses from the ECMM have attended, and they were at all of those sites where the exchanges took place, and yet these videos were not shown to those witnesses to see whether they could identify the persons involved and whether that was an accurate depiction of what took place on the day. And in our view, those witnesses should have been used and the fact that they -- they haven't means, in our submission, that those clips cannot be admitted at this stage, save for a witness being called to -- to identify them. Also, as Mr. Bourgon has pointed out, we might be able to recognise the outside of the church at Guca Gora, but unless somebody is able to identify what the church looks like on the inside and what we see is indeed what is happening on the inside - and there may well have been witnesses who could have done that - in our submission, it's not sufficient that the video be introduced as something that speaks for itself, because it might not be an accurate depiction of what occurred or what -- what was indeed the situation at the time. Your Honour, there are also scenes that are clearly not ones that may in any way speak for themselves. There was a very good example of this when General Reinhardt testified, and he was -- he was asked in cross-examination about certain troops that were identified on a clip in the video whether he could as a result of looking at the video specify which were the -- the units involved, and he said that he could not. And this was a very good example, in our view, of how when one looked at the transcript and it mentioned "Muslim forces" in the transcript, what the narrator was saying, and compared that then with what was on the -- the video itself, there was no correlation. The transcript might have said "Muslim forces," but on the video that could be a depiction of troops from any unit, and that was a -- a point that General Reinhardt agreed with. He said he couldn't exclude the fact that those pictures could be of any particular unit. So those clips, in our view, do not speak for themselves, and we cannot rely upon what the narrator has said to give them any more credence. Likewise with the scenes that are apparently about Mehurici. There's no outside confirmation, in addition to what the narrator has said, which confirms that that is indeed Mehurici and that is a training camp for the Mujahedin and what we see are in fact Mujahedin at Mehurici. It's simply what the -- the narrator has said, but the pictures do not in any way speak for themselves. So even though there might be some parts that appear reliable, in our submission, Your Honours still need to have a witness for those sections and the parts surrounding them, but in addition to that, there -- and this is by far the majority of the video, it doesn't speak for itself and one cannot rely upon, in our view, the points that are made by the narrator in order to give the scenes that we see any -- any more authenticity. So in our view, our position remains that the video as a whole should -- should not be admitted, unless witnesses are brought to speak to particular portions of the video. And there are, in our submission, witnesses who could have been brought to do that, allowing the Defence to cross-examine those witnesses and Your Honours to ask questions, or future witnesses must be called. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Dixon. Would the Prosecution like to take the floor to respond to what the Defence has just said?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The Prosecution has stated from the outset, from the very beginning, that the source -- the author of this videotape is not known, and yeah, the Prosecution was facing a kind of general problem, and this general problem, if Your Honours allow me to use these terms, is the nature of the beast. What do I mean with this? That the Mujahedin organisation as such was using covert methods, was basically trying, what can be seen also on the video, to protect certain people who belonged to this organisation by basically distorting faces and so on. So there is none of the documents on our exhibit list coming directly from the Mujahedin, we even are not aware whether the Mujahedin have produced documents, where they went to, and so on and so forth. This video, in other words, is one of the scale of the rare exhibits which we could find through our investigations. We are not in a position to provide the author of this tape, but in the Prosecution's view it makes sense that we are -- that we are not in a position to provide this information because the organisation as such is used to work by these means and puts an emphasis on -- yeah, not to reveal their identity. For example, in the Zenica prisoner exchange, which was shown on the tape, all of the Mujahedin were wearing basically masks, which just showed the mouth and the two eyes. So the very methods of this organisation obviously is not to reveal their identity. And the very reason why this tape was brought forward is that it's, as I pointed out, one of the rare instances where the Prosecution could get hold of a video which is with 113 minutes a long video. It's not a two-minutes clip which we are talking about, but, rather, we are talking about a lengthy clip, which allows the drawing of inferences and so on. And it also, in the Prosecution's view, shows the understanding of this group. And if I take this as the basis, the understanding of this group, yes, as the Defence has pointed out, the narrator -- or the narrator's voice and the text which is stated by this voice sometimes does not correspond to the images being shown, but altogether the Prosecution is of the position that, first of all, the narrator tries to give a chronological evolution of the events as they unfolded, and also in several instances, like with the Zenica prisoner exchange, like Guca Gora, the images shown there, and, for example, the Zivko Totic incident, there Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. are quite direct relationships between the story brought forward by the narrator and the images being displayed at the same time. Your Honours, this is a circumstantial case, and the Prosecution will try in the remaining time to link certain excerpts which were shown on this lengthy tape to other documents which we have on our exhibit list or link to other videotapes, which will be broadcasted in the order of today or tomorrow, since as I pointed out, the group is basically using covert methods, the Prosecution sees no other possibility than to do this. This is for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll have our break now, since it's half past 12.00, and we'll resume at five to 1.00 and we'll have 45 minutes then. You're on your feet because we're having the break now. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's continue. We have another three-quarters of an hour. The hearing is resumed, and we're going to have time for the next video. But before that, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd just like to make some remarks with respect to what my learned colleague of the Prosecution just said, his remarks to the nature of the group, basically using covert or covered methods. And, Mr. President, the nature of the group, according to the Defence's view, if it is important, must be established by producing a witness. He could come in and tell us what the nature of this Mujahedin group is and the number of experts and people who say they're experts on the subject could come before the Court and tell us if this is important enough for the Prosecution, because otherwise, Mr. President, I don't think we must take an assertion made by the Prosecution that a group was using covert or covered methods as being that, unless we have somebody to bear that out. We had numerous names mentioned, even the name of the organisation that produced this video and mentioned in the transcript, but I don't think it was a covert or covered organisation of any kind, so there's no need to make a phantom or spectacle of this group, because there's precise information. All this can be presented through a witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bourgon. Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I could just add on to that as well. My learned friend has said that there are uncertainties regarding the source of this video because that is typical of the way in which the Mujahedin operated. And admits that is one of the excuses that is offered, and that they wouldn't make the sources of this information known because they don't want that to be public. And yet, if we look at the video itself, it's not as though in the content of -- of that video the persons involved are seeking to keep their identities unknown. The names of people are mentioned; photographs appear in the video; even the daughter of one of the persons, as Your Honour noted, appeared in the video itself. So material itself -- there was no attempt by the makers to keep that from the public. And our question is whether or not it was possible through the investigations on the part of the Prosecution to get more information about who produced this video and what the purpose of the production of the video was as well. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the Prosecution like to respond and take the floor again, in view of the observations made by the Defence? Would you wish to continue and have us see the next tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecution has attempted to identify the originator of this video, but all information available to the Prosecution has been provided so far. Just as a general remark, not necessarily relating to this tape but to also other tapes coming -- or dealing with Mujahedin, sequences on the Mujahedin, some submitters have indicated to us that they don't want to have their identity revealed because they might come under threats. This, however, wasn't the case in relation to this tape. If I may just seize the opportunity and point one -- point to one section, which was screened to this tape, and just point your attention to two or three documents which can corroborate what was said on this tape. If you go to tab number 1 and page 29 of the transcript. It's about the middle of the page. It says: "English voice-over," and then it says: "The Mujahedin leadership got together to establish the reasons for the defeats and withdrawals." And then continues: "Later on" -- with the words, "the Shura council for the Mujahedin decided to stop taking part with the army in any of the military operations until the Mujahedin were recognised as an independent battalion within the Bosnian army." It then goes on: "The Bosnian army acknowledged the role that the Mujahedin had played so far and their need for men of this kind. Therefore, the Bosnian army leadership agreed to their request and recognised the Mujahedin battalion as a part of the Bosnian army over which the banner of/inaudible/could be raised." With three documents which are on the exhibit list we could quickly try to substantiate what the speaker was referring to or we could even try to find a date for this sequence -- for this event the speaker is talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It would be best to have a viewing of the next videotape first, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours want to deal with this at a later stage. I understand. So we will then go on with the video screening. The next sequence is relating to the crime site after the abduction of Zivko Totic. It has been shown already to the witness Zivko Totic, and since we are already so advanced in time, I propose to skip this sequence in order to save time, since it has been shown already, and move on to 2.2, which is relating to the video V0002452. This is a broadcast from TV Vitez breaking news about the announcement of the kidnapping of Zivko Totic. It dates from the 15th of April, 1993. The author, as I have said, is TV Vitez. It was submitted to the ICTY in the Kordic and Cerkez case by the Defence team and was introduced as Defence Exhibit D215/1 and adopted Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. in the proceedings by the witness Slavko Pavlovic. I think it was the 15th of May, 2000. And for the benefit of the Trial Chamber and the parties, the transcript, the relevant portion, can be found on pages 18.676 till pages 18.684. The duration of the excerpt - we don't play the whole tape - is about four -- is about five minutes. The tape will be played now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Nothing from the Defence? Let's go ahead, then.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] The news. Dear viewers of TV Vitez, good evening. The most important news is the serious crime that was committed today around 8.00 a.m. in Zenica, when the vehicle in which Mr. Zivko Totic, the commander of the Jure Frencetic Brigade, was driving towards the HVO command in Zenica, was attacked. The commander's escorts, Ivica Vidovic, Anto Zrnic, Marko and Tihomir, were treacherously killed in that attack. A passer-by, whose identity as yet I know, was also killed. The commander of the Jure Francetic Brigade was abducted and his whereabouts and fate are unknown. According to the latest information we received, there is no shooting in Zenica, but the situation is very tense. In connection with this, a special press conference was held today in Busovaca that you could have watched earlier. For all those of you who were not able to see this press conference, we will air it again after the "Slikom na Sliku" telecast. A proclamation by the OZCB, Operative Zone for Central Bosnia, was read out at the conference and we will show it in its entirety during this newscast. Extremist Muslim forces, under the command of the 3rd Corps of the BiH army, led by Enver Hadzihasanovic, have activated plans for murdering officers and leaders of the HVO in the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. Their goals are simple: Provoke a large-scale conflict between the ABiH and the HVO, destroy the HVO, and prevent the implementation of the Vance-Owen Agreement on the organisation of provinces signed in New York. Those calling themselves members of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina are burning Croatian flags on the eve of the Easter holidays, threatening Croats, looting, killing Croat officers and carrying out abductions, while at the same time talking about the joint struggle against the Chetniks, only distancing themselves from the perpetrators of crimes. In these difficult times of Croat history, we are calling upon the Croatian people and members of the HVO to resolutely defend our lands and our homes. We have the ability to vanquish any enemy. We are denouncing terrorist acts of extremist Muslim forces and in the interests of peace ask that all Mujahedin be expelled from these parts. We have also received public announcement from the HVO Novi Travnik on the occasion of the proclamation of the Democratic Action Party for Novi Travnik and the so-called Free City of Novi Travnik on April the 14th, 1993. The HVO of Novi Travnik issues the following announcement: In conditions of the deteriorating security situation in the territory of the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna and particularly in Novi Travnik, caused by the brazen abduction of four HVO members by members of the Muslim forces, we have again seen the dissemination of malicious and false information to the public. First, it is a brazen lie that the abduction took place in the area under HVO control; second, it is also a brazen lie that perpetrators of this crime are not known, because the HVO has received information that this was done by members of the Muslim forces; third, it is also a brazen lie that members of the HVO are staging a demonstration of force in the streets of Novi Travnik and harassing the Muslim population. All of this clearly indicates that the intention was to provoke a conflict in a wider area. The events in other municipalities of the HZ HB support this assertion. Such manner of disseminating information by leaders of the SDA Novi Travnik party and members of the Muslim forces is irritating the Croatian population and is not conducive to peace and coexistence in these parts, as well as to the implementation of signed agreements of the peace plan. Signed, the President of the Croatian Defence Council of Novi Travnik, Mr. Jozo Sekic. The aggressor was active yesterday and last night on the Travnik front. There was some fire from infantry arms from 6.00 a.m. to 1.00 p.m. along the defence lines. At 3.00 p.m. a recoilless gun and mortars opened fire on the centre of Turbe. There was no significant activity overnight. In yesterday's aggressor's action, one member of the HVO was lightly wounded. New material damage was caused by yesterday's aggressor's activity. The 59th Session of the HVO Travnik government was convened yesterday at 1.00 p.m, chaired by Mr. Zeljko Pervan. At the beginning of the session, minutes of previous meetings were adopted. Then the report on reasons for vacating the Prahulje warehouse by the UNHCR was discussed, along with group and individual responsibility on this matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This was the excerpt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We saw a five-minute excerpt, and there were two announcers. They were reading apparently text that had been prepared in advance of the news relating to the abduction of Mr. Totic, the commander of the HVO. We do not know in viewing this excerpt whether the two announcers were sitting next to each other or perhaps there were other sequences of broadcasts that were made at the time. So as there were two journalists, when there are two journalists, we can see them sitting next to each other, but here we see the announcers one following the other. So this is a juxtaposition of information given and presented at the time, during that time. When we heard the first announcer, she spoke about the abduction without giving any specific details. The second lady announcer directly mentioned the part played by the Bosnia-Herzegovina army, the ABiH, and the first announcer that comes back to us later on, succeeding the second, goes back to that issue and follows on from what the second announcer was saying. The second announcer then once again speaks about the proclamation of the HVO of Novi Travnik, which seems to be less linked to the abduction of Mr. Totic. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. So that is what we were able to see during those five minutes. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Just rapidly concerning that excerpt, the video. The first commentary is this: My learned friends of the Prosecution told the Chamber the numbers of the pages in the Kordic trial, the transcript numbers, where it seems that this video was presented by one of the Defence teams. I have taken note that the transcript in the [indiscernible] does not make up part of the evidence that we ourselves had admitted during this present trial, so those pages are not part of our own exhibits. As far as the video itself is concerned, we took note of the fact that the people on our screens, the ladies on our screens, read prepared texts, and it seems that the authors are known, but once again we have no witness coming in to authenticate this fact; that is to say, that the news reports were broadcast by the Vitez radio stations. And I think that a number of witnesses could have come in to say, "Yes, that was indeed a broadcast that was televised," but we have had no such witnesses come forward. So it was a news broadcast by Television Vitez and officially televised. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have nothing further to add to what Mr. Bourgon has said and the comments that have been made by Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the Prosecution like to respond and address the issues brought up by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just briefly, Your Honours. We have accessed the transcript excerpt just referred to, and if I may summarise briefly. Slavko Pavlovic stated that basically he had seen this sequence or he had -- yeah, seen and heard this sequence and -- on the day when it was announced. He said it was broadcast twice: In the morning, and at 7.00 p.m. in the evening in a show - if I pronounce this correctly - "Slikom na Sliko." And this sequence was just shown to demonstrate the so-to-speak knowledge or propaganda of the other side after Zivko Totic was abducted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would just like to draw the attention of the Chamber to the fact that that is precisely the objective of our comments; that is to say, that what our colleague has just told us cannot be taken as being testimony by a member of the Prosecution. We either have to have the witness before the Trial Chamber or we have to ask for admissibility of part of the Kordic proceedings pursuant to Rule 92 bis (D). Otherwise, we cannot have the Prosecution provide us with this information. Now, the videotapes that we have been viewing since yesterday and that we're still viewing have been around for many years and mostly the objections that we make have to do with the way in which the evidence has been presented. There is a method and procedure to be applied, and it is our task as Defence counsels that when that procedure is not followed, that we should take a note of that and say that there are shortcomings in the procedure of presenting this kind of evidence. So we don't wish to be any impediment to showing this evidence but just that the procedure be respected and applied as it should be. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's move on to the next tape now, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next tape is drawn from the ERN number V0002401 and the exact date is at sometime between the 15th of April, 1993 and the 17th of May, 1993, which is the time period in which the witness Zivko Totic was abducted and exchanged. The tape itself contains a message which was broadcasted -- or which was taken from Zivko Totic while he was in detention. In terms of the author -- before I mention the author, I would like to go into closed session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Closed session, Mr. Registrar, please, or private session, rather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are in open session. Let's go ahead with the videotape.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The tape will be played now, and it was already introduced into evidence as P69, but not this excerpt.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: [Voiceover] I am Zivko Totic, the commander of the HVO's Jure Francetic Brigade from Zenica. On this occasion, I am addressing the public of the town of Zenica and the region to tell the international organisations and the International Red Cross in particular that I am alive and healthy. As it is known, on the 15th of April, 1993, around 0755 hours, on Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. my regular route to my job I was abducted, kidnapped by unknown persons in the village of Podbrijezje. Two days later I was informed that on that occasion two escorts and two drivers were killed. I take this opportunity to express my condolences to the victims' families. What I want to say now is that I am particularly addressing the institution of the Herceg-Bosna's HVO with a request, and at the request of the International Red Cross, that our exchange be carried out as soon as possible, fully observing the release of all detained foreign citizens who have come to Bosnia-Herzegovina to defend it. On this occasion I also want to say that during the abduction or kidnapping I was not wounded but only injured in the head during the transport to the destination, and I do not know the place where I am now and this is my first address from the place unknown to me. I also take this opportunity to send greetings to my family, especially my son, Zarko, and wife, Ljubica, father, Petar and a large number of other members. I am once again addressing the legal bodies of HVO, the Central Bosnia Operations Zone and all my superiors asking them to review my request once again so that I can return to my family and units as soon as possible. I also want to point out that I wish that this agreement be fully observed so that neither side will fear whether on the next day one will be dead or alive, arrested, kidnapped, abducted or not. I wish that the alliance be confirmed between Muslims and Croats, who in this bloody war paid the Serbo-Chetnik army's aggression with a lot of suffering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Chamber takes note of the fact that the videotape lasts approximately four minutes. It is a statement made by Mr. Totic himself, and he was abducted and he is inviting the HVO authorities to do everything necessary to effect a change between him and the foreign citizens who were fighting for Bosnia-Herzegovina. That was the gist of it. Does the Defence have any observations to make? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Let's go into private session. Mr. Registrar, would you strike the name, do what is necessary to have the name struck from the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're in open session, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just in terms of the late screening of this tape. I can just mention that certainly it's -- this tape was also prepared at the time when Mr. Totic was here. At this point in time, a decision was made not to show it in court, and since then, yeah, this session here was set up to basically produce all the videotapes which are in our possession, and the Prosecution is basically doing this at the time being, and for this reason it is broadcasted now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We have ten minutes left. Perhaps we won't have the time to see another videotape, unless you have a very short one. In that case, it would be possible. If that isn't possible, you could perhaps use the time that we have to inform us of the other videos that we should be viewing tomorrow. I would like to point out that we'll have three hours and 45 minutes tomorrow. So the question is whether we will have enough time tomorrow to view the remaining videotapes, and if so, what procedure will we be following and in what order will the videos be shown?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next sequence would be 15 minutes in duration, so it is not possible to finish it today. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. There is, with regard to the three other tapes currently on the list, there is a possibility -- I don't want to say to merge them but to skip one or two of these small sequences, so that maybe just a lengthy sequence, the first one, for example, of five minutes, can be shown. And the Prosecution believes that these two transcript excerpts would enlighten the Chamber and the parties, that they are relevant and is herewith requesting to also introduce them in the current proceeding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. So there are a number of problems. First of all, you say that there are two transcripts that were made. The first cassette concerns Dusina and the second cassette concerns Vares. You have the relevant transcripts and you would like them to be admitted into evidence, as far as I understand. What is the position of the Defence? Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. The two transcripts were provided to us this morning by my colleague from the Prosecution. Having read the transcripts, we noticed two things: Firstly, the part selected relates to events about which one should cross-examine the witness in question, because it goes beyond the scope of what we were able to see in the video, so as things stand we object to having this transcript admitted into evidence, since we need to cross-examine the witness. And secondly, Mr. President, we have tried to identify the appropriate portion to save time. We have tried to select the portion that relates solely to the video. But, Mr. President, we have come to the conclusion that the only thing that this witness could do would be to confirm the identity of Mr. Zvonko Rajic. But yesterday, Mr. President, the Defence suggested that one should accept the fact that Mr. Zvonko Rajic is deceased. This isn't a matter that is in dispute. The matters that are in dispute concerns the nature of the wounds, concerns the site where he was killed, and concerns the manner of his killing. The video does not in any way assist the Chamber to decide anything about the matters in dispute. And if we agreed to take a very specific part of the transcript from the Kordic case, this would not assist the Chamber with regard to the video itself. So for these two reasons, Mr. President, because of the extent of the transcript, the scope of the transcript, and the fact that it wouldn't help us with regard to the video, we believe, Mr. President, that this transcript shouldn't be admitted pursuant to Rule 92 bis and it can in no way help us in relation to the video. My colleague would like to address the matter of the second video, which concerns Vares, since this is something that does not concern the accused whom I represent. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Dixon.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We would also object on the same grounds as Mr. Bourgon has outlined, in particular in relation to the second witness who was allegedly one of the refugees that fled from Vares. He was shown the same video of the alleged looting in Vares and he identified this as scenes, was his words, "scenes from Vares." But it's not clear from the transcript, having read it now that, he was actually able to identify any of the particular images that we saw or any of the particular soldiers who may have been involved in -- in that action. So for that reason, we don't believe he could be of any assistance to Your Honours. In any event, if he was going to speak to the scenes in the video, we would -- we would require him to be present in order to cross-examine him, particularly on who was involved, because that is the key issue with regard to the alleged looting in Vares. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber will inform you of our decision on the transcripts of the Dusina and Vares videos. I'll address the first point. You said that as far as tomorrow's hearing was concerned, we'll have a two-minute cassette of poor quality, a 15-minute tape as well, and then there will be a tape on destruction that lasts for about 30 minutes, and the final videotape has to do with detention facilities. You haven't told us how long this lasts. The number -- the final number of the video on detention facilities is 3971, but what is its duration?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the duration of this final videotape would be, to be precise, 79 -- 97 minutes. And for this reason, we have already approached the Defence. We are trying to either not display it at all, in order to save time, or to just display portions of it. However, the video, the way it was produced basically features all detention Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. facilities contained in the indictment, and it will be rather difficult to downsize it. It would just mean that certain views from the detention facilities or from certain rooms would need to be taken out, but I hope this will -- this problem will be solved in discussion with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will discuss the matter with the Defence. But when I add up the minutes you mentioned, we should have time, because we have three hours 45 minutes tomorrow, so we should have sufficient time, provided that the Defence doesn't take up too much time when expressing its position. And the Defence has also stated that after all the videos have been shown, they would like to make some comments of a general kind. I don't know whether these general comments could be made at the end of the hearing on Friday or whether they could be made on Monday. We'll see. But given the time we have at our disposal, I think it's necessary to see all the cassettes. If all the detention facilities appear in the cassette, it's not necessary to make a selection. Try to discuss this issue, but given the time we have, we should be able to see everything, and if necessary, the Defence's comments could be made on Monday. Mr. Mundis could perhaps inform us of the schedule for next week, since I'm not aware of it at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, as previously indicated, we are continuing to endeavour to make a witness or witnesses available for next week; however, as of the latest information I received from Mrs. Benjamin in Bosnia is that no witness has been identified who would be available to testify next week. I anticipate that she will be phoning me again this afternoon after we're out of court, and any information that I do receive from her will be relayed both to the Defence and to the Trial Chamber via the legal officer. Clearly if she does return with any witness statements or information from the archivists, that information will need to be provided in both one of the official languages and in B/C/S to the Defence as quickly as possible, and of course that may hinder our ability to get any of these witnesses here early next week. So as of right now, Mr. President, I am not in a position to make any witnesses available next week; however, we continue to take steps to make witness or witnesses available, and the parties and Trial Chamber will be informed as soon as I have any information in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If we have no witnesses, we will -- the Judges will discuss this issue, but in order to hold hearings, we could continue to view the videos that are on the so-called reserve list. How many hours of videotape on the reserve list do you have?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I cannot give an exact figure, but the amount of minutes will not be extensive. I expect rather the opposite, because some of these videos just relate to either duplicates which have already been shown, more extensive duplicates; they relate to foreign news information about the events taking place in Bosnia-Herzegovina and do therefore - not substantially - add to the enlightening of the Chamber. They, rather, present an outside view. There is, for example, also another video on destruction of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. houses. The Prosecution has made efforts to identify the villages where the destruction -- the destructed houses were shown, and it has proven to be very, very difficult to link specific scenes, destroyed houses, to certain villages, and for this reason the Prosecution is considering not to show certain videos.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Everything will be clearer tomorrow. As I said, we will continue to view the remaining videos tomorrow. We have worked a little longer than usual, but I would like to thank you and I will see everyone tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
